entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] Mud-slinging? Sheikh Hamid Rasaei, protesting his ten-month prison sentence,…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @ahmadzeidabad

Mud-slinging? Sheikh Hamid Rasaei, protesting his ten-month prison sentence, wrote a letter of objection — and Tasnim News Agency labeled it "mud-slinging against a judicial ruling" and treated it as a crime! Setting aside any judgment about the form and content of Mr. Rasaei's sentence or whether his protest letter is accurate or not, the way Tasnim News Agency has inserted itself into this affair is wrong on every count. It's as if, in this news agency's view, every judicial ruling is inherently just — even sacred — and any criticism or objection to it amounts to mud-slinging and a crime! Every day, across the entire country, thousands of judicial rulings are issued by different judges, and one of the parties to the dispute considers it unjust and tyrannical and objects to it. Are all of them committing mud-slinging and a crime? The head of the judiciary, under Article 477 of the Criminal Procedure Code, identifies several judicial rulings each month as clearly contrary to Sharia and refers them to the Supreme Court for retrial. Should the head of the judiciary's determination that a judicial ruling clearly contradicts Sharia standards be considered mud-slinging against a judicial ruling and a criminal act? Judges are human too, and even if they care about fairness and justice, they may issue a wrong ruling for thousands of reasons. Meanwhile, some of them have no concern for justice at all and are mired in the very same corruption that afflicts other employees of various institutions! The clearest, most undeniable example is Saeed Mortazavi, who for a time held sway over people's lives, property, and reputation, and in the end the country's highest officials themselves branded him a liar and removed him from office. Unfortunately, during his tenure, the possibility of safe and free criticism of his rulings — by this very logic of Tasnim News Agency — did not exist, and this gave him such an ironclad immunity that he imagined himself all-powerful, and it ultimately ended in the Kahrizak disaster! And yet, someone worse than Saeed Mortazavi still exists, but those same false immunities prevent the country's community of legal experts from criticizing their rulings. In any case, the mindset of the likes of Tasnim News Agency unfortunately does nothing to help reform and improve the judiciary's performance, no matter who the other party may be. The purpose of this piece is not to judge the nature of Mr. Rasaei's sentence or to defend his actions, which in my view are mostly sensationalist and wrong. The aim is to defend his right to object to his sentence — a right that is natural and God-given, and that even current laws recognize for every single citizen, whatever their station, yet it seems some are trying to take it away. #احمد_زیدآبادی @ahmadzeidabad

Masoud Pezeshkian has presumably prepared the text of his…

The logical point

Masoud Pezeshkian has presumably prepared the text of his speech for addressing the UN General Assembly, and it is unlikely that he would change it for any reason.

If I were in his place, however, I would try to occupy the "logical" position so that no justification remains for exerting pressure on the country.

The perennial issue confronting the Islamic Republic has been whether it is, in and of itself, a threat to some countries, or whether some countries are a threat to it.

If the president believes in the latter, he must state it explicitly and, for example, say: the Islamic Republic, in and of itself, is not hostile to any country in this world, and absent threats from them, all the problems that have arisen can be resolved within the framework of international laws, regulations, and norms. A clear, unambiguous, and unqualified declaration of this single point is occupying the logical position, and it will be met with a welcome from the general body of countries.

Uttering vague, general, and ambiguous sentences with the aim of satisfying all the disparate domestic forces will yield nothing but the hardship of a long journey.

#Ahmad_Zeidabadi

entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] A benevolent and cautious authority. I have heard valuable insights from…

Source: @ahmadzeidabad

A benevolent and cautious authority. I have heard valuable insights from Gholamhossein Karbaschi about the political and jurisprudential approach and personal character of Ayatollah Seyyed Mousa Shobeiri Zanjani. In the late 1340s and early 1350s, Mr. Karbaschi was one of the distinguished students of the late Mr. Shobeiri. According to what I have heard, Ayatollah Shobeiri was cautious in both jurisprudence and politics — the very principle that traditional Shia scholars regarded as a sign of piety. Caution means examining a matter from all sides before expressing an opinion or taking action — in other words, never wading into water without first finding a crossing — which is precisely what some clerics claiming revolutionary fervor have completely abandoned and cast aside! A cautious authority is extremely watchful of his tongue and his actions, is not one for controversy, does not level accusations against others, and for this reason is usually silent or very taciturn. The late Mr. Shobeiri, in addition to this, was inclined toward tolerance and benevolence in political matters. Although he did not speak of it, in practice he would act to the best of his ability to redress injustice or to free from political entanglement those he knew closely. In 1397, the presence of the late Ayatollah Shobeiri at the home of Sheikh Abdullah Nouri, along with the presence of Seyyed Mohammad Khatami, provoked the anger of Sheikh Mohammad Yazdi in his capacity as "Secretary of the Supreme Council of the Seminary"! Mr. Yazdi, who despite a decade of heading the Judiciary had gained no share of self-restraint, publicly reproached an authority who, in terms of jurisprudential stature, was far above him, asking why he had gone to visit people like Khatami and Nouri without his permission! [ahmadzeidabad] Unipolar and multipolar!
Has the world order ever been unipolar? Some call the…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @ahmadzeidabad

Unipolar and multipolar!

Has the world order ever been unipolar? Some call the order of the years following the collapse of the Soviet Union unipolar, but the reality is otherwise. In my view, the world has never seen a unipolar order and never will!

Is the world now heading toward a multipolar order? In my view, a "multipolar order" is the most dangerous possible state for the world, because it is not order at all — it is the very essence of disorder and instability! The emergence of a hypothetical multipolar situation in the world would mean the end of our world through devastating wars waged with weapons of mass destruction! When we speak of a "pole," the conflict of interests is its most important defining feature. The conflict of interests ultimately leads to war, leaving destruction and annihilation in its wake. If, to avoid war, a mechanism for resolving disputes were defined, then in its light the very concept of a pole would fade — because a dispute-resolution mechanism is nothing other than the definition and pursuit of common interests, and once common interests come into play, the pole loses its conventional meaning.

Today we are faced with a world in which every member plays a role proportionate to its own capacity. No member is uncontested, and no member is without influence.

A combination of the types and degrees of influence of approximately 200 members of the international community shapes the order of today's world. An infinitely intricate network, grounded in deep mutual interdependence among the members of the global community, has taken shape — one that renders obsolete all the traditional concepts customary in the international system.

We Iranians, whatever our political and ideological leanings, seem in our subconscious to be influenced by bipolar thinking — or rather by the dualistic worldview of our ancestors — and for this very reason we not only welcome polarization but are incapable of observing and understanding the world and its affairs except through its lens!

This outlook has darkened our view of reality and has cost us dearly.

As Rumi said:

Before your eyes you held a blue glass;
for that reason the world appeared blue to you.

I will explain more on this matter.

#احمد_زیدآبادی
@ahmadzeidabad
